  4. Use the lose / maintain / gain targets as starting guidelines.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the Mifflin-St Jeor equation?

Mifflin-St Jeor estimates basal metabolic rate (BMR) from sex, age, height and weight. It is considered one of the most accurate general formulas, but it is still an estimate — individual metabolism varies.

How is TDEE different from BMR?

Your BMR is multiplied by an activity factor (1.2 for sedentary up to 1.9 for very active) to estimate total daily energy expenditure (TDEE).

Where do the lose/gain targets come from?

The tool shows TDEE − 500 for weight loss and TDEE + 300 for weight gain — common starting guidelines, not medical advice. Consult a professional before a major diet change.
